prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After reading the full first round I keep a single-part prize on B028 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific case does not depend on our unanimous opening ranking. It rests on a complete arc from proglucagon processing and the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, through glucose-dependent insulin secretion and the central and gastric effects, to drugs with confirmed benefit in type 2 diabetes, obesity and, in large independent outcome trials, cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is stable, replicated and not premature. A citation centred on the physiology and the active form honours the discovery the prize has traditionally rewarded, and it uses the three-name limit without needing a second part. The chair's questions have not changed my view that a one-achievement prize is the strongest option.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. Habener is outside the credited names, Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested and cannot be settled from the supplied text, and leaving out Knudsen skips the step that turned a short-lived native peptide into liraglutide and semaglutide. A committee that weighs the therapeutic step more heavily could reasonably reject this trio. I would state in the committee's reasoning that the citation is limited to physiology and the active form, so the omissions are a deliberate scope choice and not an oversight. B045 offers a cleaner June and Sadelain pairing, but it does not outweigh B028 on maturity, breadth of evidence or completeness of the arc.

responses.point: Linnarsson names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen and argues that converting native GLP-1 into a once-weekly agent needed real insight (albumin binding, DPP-4 resistance) and was not routine engineering.
responses.response: That argument is stronger than I credited in round 1, and I accept that analogue design was not routine. I still keep Mojsov in the third seat. Your own round-1 text says the Mojsov version is more defensible under a discovery-only reading, and the citation I propose is a discovery citation. Swapping Knudsen for Mojsov would remove the person who identified the active peptide and change the citation to a therapy-oriented one. If a majority prefers that framing, I would move to your trio, but the citation would have to change with it. I do not think the choice is a matter of principle, and the two sides are closer than the stated positions suggest.

responses.point: The chair moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov so that the citation rewards the hormone's physiology and active form rather than a company's drug design, and asks what threshold of support would make each side reopen the allocation.
responses.response: I agree with the reasoning behind your move. As for the threshold, if four or more members hold Drucker, Holst and Mojsov I would not reopen the allocation. I would reopen it only if the committee concludes that the citation must name the drug-development step, because then Knudsen would have to be present. On Habener, I would not add a fourth name, since the three-name limit forbids it. I would ask that the committee record that his proglucagon work is acknowledged in the reasoning, while the citation stays narrow and the priority question is kept openly unresolved.

responses.point: Sandberg places B045 and B020 as alternatives, treats a second part as hard given the three-name limit, and says neither rule nor precedent excludes an industry laureate, so the question is the nature of the contribution.
responses.response: That is a fair correction to my round-1 remark that an industry laureate changes the character of the prize. The question is the contribution, and Knudsen's is substantial. For this configuration my reason for not including her is the scope of the citation and the three-name cap, not her employer. I agree that a second part is impractical, because B028 already uses all three names, and I would not shrink B028 to make room for another part. If the committee wanted a two-part prize, I would prefer June and Sadelain for B045 over B020 on clinical maturity, but I do not recommend that this year.

responses.point: El Manira raises the concern that honouring a drug class with a very large commercial footprint could be read as rewarding commercial success, and that long-term safety and durability after discontinuation are not settled.
responses.response: I take the commercial-success concern seriously, and it is one reason I favour a citation about physiology and the active peptide, so that the award is plainly for discovery and not for market outcome. On durability, weight regain after stopping treatment and long-term safety are still being defined. This affects how we describe the therapies, but it does not weaken the physiology, which is established, and the outcome-trial benefits are already documented. I would keep the citation's wording on the therapies modest, as in enabled treatment, and not claim a cure or finished safety profile.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that a method that opens a field, as optogenetics does, is something the prize has honoured, and ranks it ahead of CAR-T.
responses.response: I accept that the prize has honoured enabling methods. I still keep B014 out of my preferred configuration and below B045 for this year. Six credited names cannot be reduced to three without leaving out someone decisive, because the priority is split between channel discovery and neuronal application. That is a credit problem that the method's undoubted impact does not solve. If the committee returns to it in a later year, I would want that attribution settled first. I remain open on ordering B045 and B020 relative to each other.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is documented well enough to justify the third seat, since the supplied text cannot settle it.
How Habener's omission should be handled. The citation can be narrow, but the committee's reasoning should acknowledge his proglucagon work.
Whether the majority will want a therapy-oriented citation, which would bring Knudsen in and change the citation wording together with the names.
Which second candidate would follow in a later year: B045 on clinical maturity with the Rosenberg and Eshhar credit questions open, or B020 on cleanest attribution but thinner translation.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal on any shortlisted ballot. My profile documents no connection to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen or any other credited name. B045 (CAR-T) and B051 (cGAS-STING) are adjacent to immunology but I infer no personal tie, and my round-1 disclosure is unchanged.
